description: From 13 to 15 May 1911, 308 Chinese people were killed in Torreón, Coahuila - roughly half the city's Chinese community - by troops aligned with Francisco I. Madero during the Revolution. The first victims were agricultural workers killed in the orchards in the early hours of 13 May. Almost 100 Chinese businesses and homes were destroyed.
energy_note: Three hundred and eight people, in ten hours.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the finding, and the diplomatic aftermath
description: An investigation concluded the massacre was an unprovoked act of racial hatred, and a military tribunal appointed by Emilio Madero found the Maderista soldiers had committed atrocities. China demanded 30 million pesos in reparations. In 2021 President López Obrador apologised, saying the objective was to ensure it never happens again.
energy_note: Apologised for, one hundred and ten years later.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the Sonora and Sinaloa expulsions, 1931-33
description: Sonora and Sinaloa were the only states to carry out mass expulsions of Chinese men and their families - including families of Mexican origin. In 1931 the Sonoran government enacted discriminatory laws effectively banishing the Chinese; the mass expulsion ran 1931 to 1933. Several thousand were deported, some directly to China, others pushed through gaps in the international boundary fence into the United States, whose agents then deported the families onward to China.
energy_note: Pushed through a hole in the border fence by their own government.

aspect: EXAMPLE - and Mexican women lost their nationality for marrying them
description: Mexican women were stripped of Mexican citizenship for marrying Chinese men. The expelled families arrived in Guangdong and eventually congregated in Macau.
energy_note: She married him and ceased to be Mexican.

aspect: Why it is in this dataset
description: It records that the state applying the hurdles in this file has itself expelled a minority by race within living memory of the grandparents of people now alive - which is context for DIS-001 and DIS-002 rather than a separate subject.
energy_note: The same state, doing the same thing, to someone else.
notes: Scholarly source: Julia María Schiavone Camacho, Chinese Mexicans (UNC Press, 2012); Julián Herbert on Torreón.
